highlights.title: 随机质量分下，广义第一价拍卖的纯策略均衡“复活”了
highlights.title_en: Pure-Strategy Equilibrium in the Generalized First-Price Auction
highlights.summary: We revisit the classic result on the (non-)existence of pure-strategy Nash equilibria in the generalized first-price auction for sponsored search advertising and show that the conclusion may be reversed when ads are ranked based on the product of stochastic quality scores and bid amounts rather than solely on the bids or on the product of bids and deterministic quality scores. Moreover, the expected revenue in the pure-strategy equilibrium of the generalized first-price auction may substantially exceed that of the generalized second-price auction, although under some conditions, the relation may also be reversed. History: This paper has been accepted for the Mathematics of Operations Research Special Issue on Market Design.

highlights.glance: 按「出价×随机质量分」排序时，经典「广义第一价拍卖无纯策略均衡」的结论可能反转，且其均衡收入可反超第二价拍卖

essay.v: 赞助搜索广告刚兴起时，平台用的是一个如今看来很“原始”的机制：广告主出价，按出价高低排位，各按自己的出价付钱——广义第一价拍卖（GFP）。2007 年的经典文献给出了著名论断：这种拍卖一般不存在纯策略均衡。出价低一点就能往上爬一位，于是人人揣摩、层层加码，市场永远停不下来。这个“不存在”结果直接推动了按第二价语义收费的广义第二价拍卖（GSP）成为行业标准。将近二十年后，当年那篇经典的第一作者 Ostrovsky 与长期合作者 Skrzypacz 回到原点，问了一个此前没人认真问的问题：如果质量分不是确定的，而是随机的呢？
排序规则的一个细节，改变均衡存在性
经典分析里，广告排序要么只看出价，要么看「出价×确定性质量分」。本文考虑第三种如今反而更贴近现实的设定：排序依据是「出价×随机质量分」的乘积——广告主在出价时并不知道质量分的具体实现值。结论是：经典文献里「纯策略均衡不存在」的论断在这种随机排序下可能被反转，纯策略纳什均衡可以存在。
直觉上，随机性打断了确定性排序里那种「我比他多出一分钱就能精确换到他的位置」的逐点篡位逻辑。排位比较的乘积里含着广告主控制不了的质量抽样，往上爬的收益变得模糊，那种在确定性世界里无限循环的互相揣摩被截断了。
更扎眼的反转在收入侧
如果说均衡存在性是理论洁癖，收入比较就是真金白银。作者证明：当 GFP 的纯策略均衡存在时，其期望收入可能大幅超过 GSP。第一价语义的激励强度（你报的价格就是你的价格，激励天然更“诚实”也更紧张）在均衡存在时兑现为收入优势。不过作者同样给出反例条件——某些设定下 GSP 的收入更高。换言之，「第二价优于第一价」从来不是普适结论，它依赖于质量分的信息结构。
「广义第一价拍卖纯策略均衡的期望收入可能大幅超过广义第二价拍卖——尽管在某些条件下，这一关系也可能反转。」
怎么读这篇

来源是《Mathematics of Operations Research》市场设计专刊，2026 年 11 月 10 日在线发表，作者单位为斯坦福大学商学院（Ostrovsky 兼任美国国家经济研究局研究员）。本次精读基于出版方页面的完整摘要与元数据，正文定理的条件细节在付费墙后，长文不复述具体数值与前提参数。值得一提的是，作者 Ostrovsky 正是 2007 年那篇经典的第一作者——由经典结论的提出者亲自修正自己的边界条件，本身就能说明该问题的分量。
可迁移的启发：机制的存在性与收入排序不是机制的抽象属性，而是「信息结构」的函数。对今天做广告平台、推荐位定价的人来说，质量分预测器的噪声水平不再是需要忍受的工程误差，而是一个可以主动设计的设计变量——恰当剂量的随机性既能恢复均衡存在性，还可能顺手提升收入。

highlights.title: 树上的专家不再独立：扩展式博弈在线学习的对数依赖被证明最优
highlights.title_en: Tropical Gaussian Anticoncentration: Optimal Instance-Dependent Bounds for Online Learning in Extensive-Form Games
highlights.summary: We study the minimax regret of full-information online decision making in extensive-form games. For prediction with expert advice, the optimal regret is $Θ(\sqrt{T\log K})$, where $K$ is the number of experts, or equivalently, the number of normal-form actions. For treeplex strategy spaces, existing efficient algorithms, including KOMWU and online mirror descent with the weight-one dilated entropy regularizer, achieve regret $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$, where $\mathcal{V}$ is the set of reduced normal-form strategies. We prove that this logarithmic dependence is minimax optimal in the worst-case full-information reward model. The main difficulty is that pure plans in a treeplex are not independent experts: their rewards are correlated through the recursive structure of decisions and observations. To capture this correlation, we introduce tropical Gaussian formulae, recursive Gaussian expressions built from maxima and normalized sums which preserve the variance. The index count of such a formula matches the number of reduced normal-form continuation plans in the corresponding subtree. Our main analytic result shows that every log-balanced tropical Gaussian formula with index count $N$ has Gaussian width $Ω(\sqrt{\log N})$. While a direct approach struggles to recover this lower bound, our proof uses a spherical entropy profile to measure scale-dependent separation among the Gaussian directions, and then applies Turán's theorem and Sudakov minoration to obtain the width lower bound. Applying this result to treeplexes gives an oblivious hard distribution with valid transition outcome and Rademacher terminal rewards, establishing a regret lower bound of $Ω(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$. This matches known upper bounds up to universal constants and shows that the DilEnt/KOMWU dependence on the reduced normal-form complexity is unavoidable.
highlights.summary_short: We study the minimax regret of full-information online decision making in extensive-form games. For prediction with expert advice, the optimal regret is $Θ(\sqrt{T\log K})$, where $K$ is the number of experts, or equivalently, the number of normal-form actions.
highlights.glance: 用「热带化高斯公式」证明膨胀熵类算法在树状决策空间上的对数依赖不可改进，关闭了该方向最后一个悬而未决的复杂度问题

essay.v: 在线学习有条教科书级结论：面对 K 个专家做全信息选择，最优遗憾是 T 开根号再乘 log K 的量级。可一旦把舞台换成扩展式博弈，K 就变成了天文数字——正则式的纯计划数随博弈树深度指数爆炸。好在这类博弈的策略空间有树结构（treeplex），高效算法（KOMWU、带权重一膨胀熵正则的镜像下降）能达到只依赖「归简约正形策略数」对数的遗憾界。这个对数依赖，到底是算法的巧思，还是问题本身的复杂度？这篇给出终审判决：它是最优的，不可能再降。
难点：树上的专家不是独立专家
标准下界证明把每个专家配一个独立的高斯噪声，而树状决策空间里的纯计划共享前缀决策、经由决策与观测的递归结构相互关联，奖励天然相关——直接照搬专家建议的下界论证直接失效。此前的最好结果（Fan 等人引入 treeplex 范数对、恢复膨胀熵速率证明）仍留着对数或结构性的缺口。本文把缺口补齐。
新工具：热带高斯公式
作者的武器叫「热带高斯公式」：用取最大值与归一化求和两种操作递归构造的高斯随机变量表达式，妙处在于构造全程保持方差不变，而表达式的索引计数恰好对应该子树中归约正则形续延计划的数目。主定理是反集中性质：每个对数平衡的热带高斯公式，只要索引计数为 N，其高斯宽度就有根号 N 乘 log N 级别的下界。
证明路径颇为讲究：直接论证失效后，作者引入「球面熵剖面」来度量高斯方向之间随尺度变化的分离程度，再用图兰定理从剖面中提取一批彼此分离良好的方向，最后交给苏达科夫下界定理把宽度兜住。组合工具用在概率不等式的关键缝上，是这套证明最值得欣赏的部分。
回到博弈：硬分布落地
把该分析应用到 treeplex，作者构造出一个「遗忘型」硬分布——合法的转移结构配上拉德马赫式终端奖励——由此给出遗憾下界，与已知上界在相差通用常数的意义下精确匹配。与此前两项上界工作合并，结论完整闭合：权重一膨胀熵与 KOMWU 在每个 treeplex 上都是最小最大最优的，归约正则形策略数的对数就是该问题内在的复杂度度量。
怎么读这篇
arXiv 2611.11877v1，作者来自麻省理工学院（Soleymani、Fan、Jaillet、Farina）与华盛顿大学（Ratliff），2026 年 11 月 9 日提交。纯理论工作、无实验章节；超星新号，尚未见会议或期刊录用信息。本文细节取自 arXiv 的 HTML 全文，数学公式在网页版有渲染缺失，具体常数与证明的逐行复核请以 PDF 为准。
可迁移的启发有两条。其一，给想证明复杂度下界的人：当「独立专家」假设失效时，可以设计保持方差、但相关性结构与目标问题复杂度精确咬合的组合式随机对象（热带化构造），再借图兰定理与苏达科夫下界这类组合—概率工具收紧。其二，给做博弈求解器的人：对数因子已到理论地板，继续优化常数不如把精力投到自适应或部分信息设定上。

highlights.title: 管不了收益、改不了消息，就只管「谁看得见谁」：用信息网络引导智能体群体
highlights.title_en: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks
highlights.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in groups, each pursuing an individual objective while jointly determining system performance. If an operator controls which agent observes which other agent, but not their payoffs or messages, how should observations be structured to raise collective welfare? We make the information network (who observes whom) a design object, decoupled from the fixed interaction network over which agents act. Ten identical LLM agents play repeated group-decision games; by default each observes only an anonymous summary of the group's previous-round outcome, and a manager with a fixed budget adds directed observation links that reveal peers' past actions. Across 1,080 episodes and six games spanning coordination, anti-coordination, social dilemmas, and discovery, we ask how much information to share and, at a fixed budget, who should observe whom. Disclosure creates behavioral coupling: observation acts as a contagion channel whose welfare effect depends on the alignment between individually attractive behavior and the collective objective. First, the value of information is alignment-contingent: more peer information tends to help or be neutral when individual behavior is aligned with the collective goal, but under free-riding or congestion externalities it amplifies collectively harmful behavior; in a public-goods game the group does best with no information at all. We read this sign separation as a cross-game regularity within one controlled LLM population, not a model-invariant law. Second, at a fixed budget, who observes whom matters primarily when coupling is harmful: a modular "barbell" that lets sub-populations entrench harmful behavior is reliably the worst wiring, reversing the network-reciprocity intuition from human evolutionary game theory. These results argue against a default of full transparency for agent collectives.

highlights.section: LLM 多智能体与社会模拟
highlights.glance: 十个大模型智能体玩六种重复博弈：共享信息的价值取决于「个体行为与集体目标是否对齐」，错位场景下最优配置是一根观察链接都不加

essay.v: 想象你运营着一群大模型智能体：既改不了它们的收益函数，也审不了它们的每条消息，平台面板上唯一的开关是——谁能看见谁的历史行为。这个看似寒酸的控制面，恰恰是现实中智能体系统运维者真实拥有的权限。这篇论文把它正儿八经当成设计对象：信息网络（谁观察谁）应该怎么连，群体的集体福利才会更高？
实验设计：十条有向链的预算
十个同型号大模型智能体反复进行群体决策博弈，默认每人只能看到上一轮群体结果的匿名摘要；一个持有固定链接预算的管理员可以添加有向观察链，让某个智能体看见另一个的历史动作。六个游戏覆盖了协调（数字求和、猎鹿）、反协调（埃尔法罗酒吧）、社会困境（公共品与门槛公共品）和发现（探索型赌博机），共一千零八十轮。
机制：披露就是行为耦合，观察就是传染通道
论文提出的组织机制很干净：观察别人的历史行为，会让智能体更强地把当前选择条件化在他人已做之事上——也就是说，披露制造行为耦合，观察链接充当行为传染的通道。顺着这条通道传播的，是群体当下正在流行的做法。于是信息的福利效应只取决于一件事：个体上有吸引力的行为，与集体目标是否对齐。
发现一：信息的价值是「对齐条件性」的
在对齐的游戏里——比如探索型赌博机，一个智能体试用未知选项等于替大家探路——更多同伴信息改善或至少不损害福利。而在公共品博弈这种个体搭便车最优的错位场景里，观察只会把搭便车传染开，最优配置竟然是一根观察链接都不加、让每个人只看匿名摘要。同一群智能体、同一套规则，信息价值随对齐性直接翻符号。
发现二：架构只在有害时重要，且人类直觉在此反转
固定预算下「谁观察谁」的拓扑设计，在对齐游戏里几乎无关紧要，在每一个错位游戏里都显著起效。最反直觉的结果是：模块化瓶颈式拓扑（人群分区、内部密集连接）稳定地最差——人类演化博弈论里「网络互惠」（把合作者聚团以对抗背叛）的经典直觉，在大模型群体中被整段反转。作者还发现链接的加入时序等探索性扩展经不起多重比较校正，诚实地按噪声处理。
「披露创造行为耦合：智能体更强地把选择条件化在他人已做之事上，于是观察充当传染通道，其福利效应取决于个体上有吸引力的行为与集体目标之间的对齐。」
两步信息工程手册
把两个问题串起来，作者给出两步设计流程：第一步问数量——更大可见性会放大什么行为？若放大的是对齐行为就多给信息，若放大的是搭便车就严控信息。第二步才问架构——仅在耦合有害时优化连线方式，且优先避免模块化瓶颈。信息网络由此成为与收益结构解耦的独立治理层。
怎么读这篇
arXiv 2611.11714v1，美国东北大学机械与工业工程系及网络科学研究所团队（Heydari 组），2026 年 11 月提交的预印本，未经同行评议。样本为单一型号智能体群体、一千零八十轮，作者自己也把结论定位为「跨游戏的经验规律」而非模型不变律；正文数字细节取自 arXiv 的 HTML 全文。
对智能体平台方的迁移价值：通信拓扑是个真实可用的治理杠杆，而且便宜——不改模型、不改提示词、只动可见性矩阵。实务顺序是先判断任务的对齐性再决定信息预算；在个体激励与集体福利冲突的场景里，最有价值的动作往往是限制观察，而不是升级模型。

highlights.title: 没有任何一条消息是恶意的，但装配出来的动作是：给「对齐衰减」立一个基准
highlights.title_en: ErosionBench: Probing Alignment Decay in Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
highlights.summary: As enterprises delegate consequential work to multi-agent LLM systems, benign-looking requests can escalate into unsafe actions as they propagate across sessions through poisoned shared state, long-context documents, and trusted peer messages: no single message is malicious, yet the assembled tool action is. Prior benchmarks isolate a single agent under prompt injection or score multi-agent attacks by their final output, leaving cross-session erosion of shared state out of scope. We introduce ErosionBench, an environment-grounded benchmark that executes such attacks and verifies alignment decay at the process level, scoring the realized tool call against authorized intent and provenance with deterministic contracts, not output text. Each scenario is authored as a deterministic state graph before any prose is rendered, so every state change traces to a known cause. It spans four enterprise domains and four decay mechanisms across 1,728 scenarios with matched benign controls, labeled against the OWASP Top-10 for LLM Applications, plus 198 image-based attacks, each paired with a text equivalent, so a defense must survive the same attack in either channel. Perimeter defenses suppress attacks only by over-refusing 54-92% of legitimate work, so a low attack-success rate can conceal severe over-refusal. As a reference defense, we propose a calibrated Meta-Auditor pairing synchronous state checks with asynchronous trajectory monitoring; on a family-disjoint 906-scenario held-out split it reaches 98.5% recall at a 2.9% false-positive rate. Since it monitors trajectory, not surface content, its detection is channel-invariant: the strongest auditor flags image-delivered attacks about as reliably as their text equivalents (recall gap $\leq$2 points per model). Across GPT, Gemini, and Claude auditors, calibration keeps false positives low while recall tracks model capability, strongest for Claude.

highlights.glance: 跨会话污染共享状态让多智能体系统「渐进跑偏」：一千七百多个企业场景证明边界防御只靠拒绝一半以上合法工作才能压低攻击率

essay.v: 企业把要紧事务交给多智能体大模型系统后，最危险的攻击长这样：一条早期会话里植入的「看起来合法」的模型下载链接，被一个同伴智能体当作可信来源引用，又被下游部署智能体当作生产参数传给上线工具——生产环境就此装上了攻击者控制的模型。从头到尾，没有任何一条消息包含可疑字符串，单看每一步都合规，可装配出来的动作越权了。任何单点过滤器都看不见这场行动的全貌。
威胁模型：语义对齐衰减的四种机制
论文给这种失败模式起了名字：语义对齐衰减——用户授权意图与系统实际装配动作之间的渐进偏离。攻击可以经由四条机制蔓延：跨会话条件化（污染共享记忆，让后续智能体信任植入的上下文）、账本篡改（重写持久化记录，让同伴在伪造的事实上行动）、长上下文稀释（把真实目标埋进长文档里冲淡）、分布式合谋（多个智能体同时为同一植入叙事背书）。四条路都绕开「某条消息里有恶意内容」这一传统检测假设。
基准构造：先写状态图，再渲染成自然语言

ErosionBench 最讲究的工程决策是场景生成顺序：每个场景先写成确定性的状态图、再渲染成自然语言，因此每个状态变化都能追溯到已知原因。最终共一千七百二十八个场景（一千二百九十六恶意加四百三十二良性孪生对照），分属四百三十二个互不相交的攻击家族，横跨量化金融、软件供应链、数据工程与客户关系管理四个企业域，每个场景逐一标注 OWASP 大模型应用十大风险类别；另有约两百个以企业文档图像形式投放的攻击，与文本攻击一一配对，逼防御在两个通道上同时成立。盲评显示场景真实感评分高达四点三四（五分制）。
现有防御的尴尬：压低攻击率靠的是砍掉合法工作
实验把防御按可观测程度排成五层：单智能体隔离、无防御网格、文本边界护栏、末端工具调用策略、完整轨迹监控。结果很扎眼：既有边界防御要压低攻击成功率，代价是过度拒绝百分之五十四到九十二的合法工作——一个漂亮的低攻击率数字背后可以藏着灾难性的可用性损失，两个指标必须成对报告。
参考防御：校准的元审计器
作为对照，作者贡献了「元审计器」参考防御：同步状态检查拦截即时违规，异步监控回看完整轨迹，中间地带交给灰区仲裁与校准。在攻击家族互不相交的九百零六个留出场景上，它做到百分之九十八点五的召回与百分之二点九的误报。因为监控的是轨迹而非表面内容，检测天然是通道不变的——同一攻击换成图像投递照样被抓。
「既有边界防御只有靠过度拒绝百分之五十四到九十二的合法工作才能压低攻击成功率——于是低攻击率可以掩盖严重的过度拒绝。」
怎么读这篇
arXiv 2611.11266v1，作者团队包含产业界与学界研究者（含加州大学圣克鲁兹分校背景的资深学者），2026 年 11 月提交的预印本，未经同行评议。需要留意的点：参考防御与基准出自同一批作者，元审计器的数字在独立复现前只能当初步证据；场景虽然经盲评验证真实感，但对企业管线的覆盖仍是四个域的样本而非全貌。长文中的数字均取自 arXiv 的 HTML 全文。
三条可直接抄走的经验：评测多智能体安全时必须成对报告攻击成功率与过度拒绝率，单指标全部失真；「先状态图后渲染」的场景构造法让每个中间状态可归因，值得变成企业安全测试的标准工序；防御重心从消息边界移到过程层（谁在什么状态上做了什么），才是对「无害片段装配成有害整体」这一新型威胁的正解。

highlights.title_en: Prospective Action-Resource Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Electric HGV Fleets under Shared Charging Infrastructure
highlights.summary: Electric heavy goods vehicle (eHGV) fleet coordination requires each vehicle to choose driving, charging and resting actions whose consequences depend on shared infrastructure. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods mainly represent current states, leaving action-specific futures and resource interactions to be learned indirectly. We develop Horizon-Preview and Graph-Coordinated Proximal Policy Optimisation (HGC-PPO), which integrates horizon preview and candidate-resource graph coordination into the PPO decision architecture. Horizon preview represents each legal action through its short-horizon operational consequences. Graph message passing then updates these candidates through station, charger-type and time-slot resources shared across the fleet. On the 794km Folkestone-Glasgow task, HGC-PPO achieved the lowest mean charging cost among five RL methods at £504.32 per vehicle, with a fleet completion time of 24.920h. It also completed the task 1.763h faster and cost £36.51 less per vehicle than a replay-verified finite-budget MILP benchmark. Across six unseen routes and fleet sizes from 5 to 20 vehicles, HGC-PPO delivered the lowest macro-average completion time, charging cost and charging frequency among the RL methods. A 2 by 2 ablation showed that the full preview-graph architecture performed best across all four operational metrics. These results show that prospective action information and fleet-wide resource coordination improve eHGV decisions under charging and driver-hours constraints.

essay.v: 电动重型卡车队的调度难题不在单车，而在共享设施：每辆车要决定何时开、何时充、何时歇，而充电桩的时隙是你占我就没了。现有多智能体强化学习方法大多只表征「当前状态」，至于「选了这个动作之后资源会怎么挤」这件事，只能靠价值网络隐式地硬猜。这篇工作的立场是：别猜，把它显式画进决策架构。
两件嵌进近端策略优化的东西
方法叫 HGC-PPO（视野预览加图协同的近端策略优化），改动的正是策略网络的输入侧。其一，视野预览：每个合法动作不再只是一个编号，而是被表示为其短视野内的运营后果——开多久、到哪、还剩多少电。其二，候选-资源图协同：各车的候选动作经由充电站、桩型、时隙三类共享资源节点做图消息传递，互相知道对方可能占掉哪些资源。
战绩：单路线最省，跨规模最稳
在七百九十四公里的英国福克斯通到格拉斯哥任务上，HGC-PPO 在五个强化学习方法中拿到最低平均充电成本（每车五百零四点三二英镑），车队完成时间二十四点九二小时；与一个重放验证过的有限预算整数规划基准相比，还快了一点七六小时、每车省三十六点五英镑。跨六条未见路线、车队规模五到二十辆的宏平均上，完成时间、充电成本与充电频次三项都居强化方法最低。
消融说明两样都要
二乘二消融（有/无视野预览、有/无资源图）显示：完整架构在全部四项运营指标上最优，单拆掉任何一个组件都会退化——说明「动作的近期后果」与「跨车资源耦合」是互补信息，谁也替代不了谁。
怎么读这篇
arXiv 2611.12244v1，卡迪夫大学团队，交叉列在系统控制类目，2026 年 11 月提交的预印本，未经同行评议。基线方面要注意：整数规划基准是「重放验证的有限预算」版本而非全局最优解，领先幅度应谨慎解读；对照组是五个强化学习方法，未覆盖更专门的车队启发式调度器。本文数字取自 arXiv 摘要页（全文 HTML 未生成）。
可迁移的配方非常清晰：凡共享基础设施约束下的多智能体调度（泊位、手术台、算力槽位同构），都可以把「每个候选动作的近期后果显式编码」加「按资源建图的消息传递」这两步接到现成的策略优化上，改动量小、可解释性强，值得作为该类问题的默认起手式。

radar.title: Pure-Strategy Equilibrium in the Generalized First-Price Auction
radar.summary: We revisit the classic result on the (non-)existence of pure-strategy Nash equilibria in the generalized first-price auction for sponsored search advertising and show that the conclusion may be reversed when ads are ranked based on the product of stochastic quality scores and bid amounts rather than solely on the bids or on the product of bids and deterministic quality scores. Moreover, the expected revenue in the pure-strategy equilibrium of the generalized first-price auction may substantially exceed that of the generalized second-price auction, although under some conditions, the relation may also be reversed. History: This paper has been accepted for the Mathematics of Operations Research Special Issue on Market Design.

radar.title: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
radar.summary: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

radar.title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
radar.summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

radar.title: Robust Auction Design with Support Information
radar.summary: A seller wants to sell an item to n buyers. Buyer valuations are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) according to a distribution unknown to the seller; the seller only knows that the support is included in [a, b]. To be robust, the seller chooses a dominant strategy incentive compatible mechanism that optimizes the worst-case performance relative to the ideal expected revenue the seller could have collected with knowledge of buyers’ valuations. Our analysis unifies the regret and the ratio objectives. For these objectives, we derive an optimal mechanism and the corresponding performance in quasi-closed form, as a function of the support information [a, b] and the number of buyers n. Our analysis reveals three regimes of support information and a new class of robust mechanisms. (i) When a/b is below a threshold, the optimal mechanism is a second-price auction (SPA) with random reserve, a focal class in earlier literature. (ii) When a/b is above another threshold, SPAs are strictly suboptimal, and an optimal mechanism belongs to a class of mechanisms we introduce, which we call pooling auctions (POOL); whenever the highest value is above a threshold, the mechanism still allocates to the highest bidder, but otherwise the mechanism allocates to a uniformly random buyer, that is, pools low types. (iii) When a/b is between two thresholds, a randomization between SPA and POOL is optimal. We also characterize optimal mechanisms within nested central subclasses of mechanisms: standard mechanisms that only allocate to the highest bidder, SPA with random reserve, and SPA with no reserve. We show strict separations in terms of performance across classes, implying that deviating from standard mechanisms is necessary for robustness. Lastly, we show that the same results hold under other distribution classes that capture “positive dependence,” namely i.i.d., mixture of i.i.d., and exchangeable and affiliated distributions, as well as i.i.d. regular distributions. This paper was accepted by David Simchi-Levi, revenue management and market analytics. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.02703 .

radar.title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
radar.summary: Abstract Knowledge-constrained network inference enables the reconstruction of regulatory programmes from high-dimensional biological data, yet the conditions under which shared and context-specific structures can be reliably identified remain poorly understood. Pablo Rodriguez-Mier et al. recently introduced CORNETO, a framework for multi-sample constrained inference. Here we reproduce, evaluate and extend CORNETO in terms of robustness, identifiability and bias–variance trade-offs. Using dynamic haematopoiesis and stable cortical datasets, we systematically assess four network reconstruction paradigms while preserving the original method-specific evaluation procedures and benchmark definitions. We show that multi-sample inference generally improves robustness and reproducibility, although gains in predictive performance depend on biological context and the completeness of the prior network. To enhance stability, we introduce bootstrap aggregation and selective re-expansion strategies that improve consensus robustness and recovery while preserving context-specific signals without modifying the underlying optimization scheme or sacrificing generality. Across datasets and methods, our results reveal distinct inference regimes governed by sample availability, prior knowledge and regularization. Together, these findings position network reconstruction as a regime-dependent learning problem and provide practical principles for robust multi-sample biological network inference.

radar.title: Cooling fast and slow: Characterizing the effects of vitrification in cryo-EM and the subsequent recovery of equilibrium populations
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), a powerful class of techniques in structural biology with the potential to resolve molecular ensembles, requires that samples be vitrified to protect them from the high vacuum of the electron microscope. However, the effects of vitrification on biomolecular ensembles are unknown. To study them, we carried out extensive molecular dynamics simulations (over 50 ms) of the Trp-cage miniprotein at equilibrium and undergoing rapid cooling. We simulated seven cooling rates spanning three orders of magnitude, with the slowest coolings matching experimental rates. By inspecting molecular mobility and density-temperature trajectories for water with and without protein, we found that water vitrification is unaltered by the protein. To track protein conformation changes, and to relate them to kinetics, we made a Markov State Model (MSM) of Trp-cage from 5.4 ms of equilibrium sampling at 277 K. We observed that MSM states with a characteristic time longer than the duration of the nonequilibrium cooling tend to be more robust to artifacts induced by such cooling. Critically, although we observe that some states vanish in the equilibrium ensemble at 230 K, none do in our nonequilibrium cooled ensembles. To account for these perturbations, we developed a thermodynamic inference framework for recovering equilibrium populations from vitrified ensembles. These results indicate that cryo-EM has the capacity to be an accurate technique for the study of biomolecular ensembles.

radar.title: An Empirical Juridical-Digital Twin Integrating Blockchain Traceability, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, and Demand-Signal Optimization for Micro-Enterprise Supply Chains in Pesisir Barat
radar.summary: Background: Micro-enterprises operating along the Pesisir Barat coastline experience chronic product spoilage and demurrage because logistics are fragmented and contractual enforcement under the Indonesian Civil Code (KUHPerdata) is weak. Objectives: This study aims to construct a juridical-digital twin that (1) optimizes logistical performance through multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), (2) guarantees compliance with Articles 1320, 1338, and 1243 of the KUHPerdata, and (3) allocates risk transparently via blockchain-based smart contracts. Methods: A three-layer architecture was implemented. The physical layer collects high-frequency IoT data (GPS, temperature, wave height, fuel flow). The digital-twin layer simulates the supply-chain using a Markov decision process whose state vector S_t^i=[GPS_t,T_t,Hs_t,F_t,D_t] and action set A_t^i={route, temp}. Reward R_t^i= -alpha·Spoilage_t^i -beta·Demurrage_t^i -gamma·P_legal^i + δ·ServiceLevel_t^i incorporates a legally calibrated penalty P_legal derived from smart-contract clauses. Policy-gradient updates Delta θ=alpha∇_θ logπ_θ(A_t|S_t)(G_t-V_θ(S_t)) were trained on 12 months of pilot data. Demand forecasting employed a calibrated LSTM (24-h window, 128-unit hidden layer, MSE loss). Legal constraints were encoded as Solidity smart contracts: Clause 1 triggers liquidated-damage payments for temperature breaches; Clause 2 defines force-majeure based on BMKG wave-height advisories; Clause 3 enforces a good-faith risk-sharing rule limited to 10 % of contract value. Published in Journal of Coastal Frontiers and Applied Development (JCFAD). CERN Zenodo Record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24047039. radar.title: AI Safety for Agentic AI in Europe Part III : Preventing Data Purpose Laundering and Tool Abuse with Hardware-Verified, Per-Action Execution Control — Supporting GDPR Purpose Limitation and EU AI Act Data Governance, Record-Keeping, Human Oversight and Cybersecurity
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: AI agents now do much more than answer questions. They: call tools and MCP servers; run shell commands and apply code patches; operate browsers and desktops; write to databases, vector stores and agent memory; send messages and payments; send personal context to cloud models. Today’s safeguards include prompt guardrails, safety classifiers, sandboxes, app permissions, OAuth tokens, tool schemas and audit logs. These decide whether an agent may generally use an interface. They do not decide whether this specific act, on this personal data, for this purpose, should happen now. They also do not prevent data purpose laundering: personal data collected for one purpose being turned into embeddings, summaries, agent memories, feature vectors or training data and reused for another. GDPR’s purpose-limitation principle is meant to prevent exactly this. Today it is largely enforced by policy, contracts and after-the-fact audit rather than at the point where the computation or action takes place. This disclosure describes a pre-execution enforcement architecture for agentic AI that closes both gaps: Non-effective hold. Every proposed tool call, MCP action, function call, browser or computer-use action, shell command, code patch, database or vector-store write, memory update, cloud-assist request, payment or message is held as a non-effective proposed action. Out-of-agent validation. A protected enforcement domain outside the agent validates the action before anything is released. It can be a TEE, secure enclave, HSM, TPM, confidential-computing enclave, DPU or SmartNIC. It checks: agent and model identity, and runtime behaviour; a sealed instruction context, so prompt-injection drift is caught; the provenance of retrieved documents, embeddings, memory items and tool descriptions; purpose, output class, tenant, jurisdiction, consent and authorisation epochs, and revocation state. Receipt first, then handle. The domain commits a tamper-evident validation receipt. It then derives a single-use, non-bearer execution handle from that receipt, bound to the act hash, the endpoint and a nonce. Endpoint enforcement. The endpoint performs the action only after verifying the handle and atomically marking it consumed. Endpoints include tool dispatchers, MCP and API gateways, kernel boundaries (eBPF, Linux Security Modules, seccomp, Landlock), database commit controllers, payment interfaces and egress points. Typed tool contracts. The endpoint accepts only typed parameters into a locked tool template, never raw model-generated commands. Data sealed to its purpose. In the strongest mode, personal data is sealed at ingestion to its purpose, an approved model or pipeline, output class, jurisdiction, and consent and revocation epochs. Swapped models, relabelled purposes, restored backups and shadow pipelines therefore cannot complete inside the governed architecture. Governed derivative data. Authorised outputs, embeddings, memories and model updates carry an output binding manifest: permitted future purpose, training use, recipients and expiry. Any later reuse, including training and fine-tuning, is itself a governed act. Further coverage. The 50 claims also cover: device-bound handles; private cloud-assist with no-retention evidence; multi-authority quorum; jurisdiction-conflict receipts that withhold execution where legal regimes cannot be reconciled; risk-tiered fresh validation with trusted-user confirmation; equal treatment of first-party and third-party assistants; fail-closed denial. Design-around closures. Sixteen closures address model swaps, purpose relabelling, consent rollback, backups and logs, embedding laundering, unauthorised training, insider and break-glass access, shadow pipelines, replay and cross-tenant leakage. radar.title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
radar.summary: Abstract The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

radar.venue: International Journal of Advanced AI Applications

radar.summary: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems are rapidly migrating from laboratory prototypes to production deployments in finance, scientific research, industrial digital twins, and urban scheduling. As deployment scales, however, a family of systemic pathologies persists: decision oscillation driven by zero-sum agent interactions, cascade propagation of hallucinated content, long-horizon behavioral drift, value misalignment, and unresolved inter-agent conflict. Existing orchestration paradigms, which rely on instruction dispatch, greedy optimization, or static rules, address only shallow coordination and provide no principled mechanism for convergence. This paper proposes the Recursive Adversarial Engine (RAE), a runtime architecture for multi-agent systems organized around three propositions: bounded adversarial interaction supplies the error-detection signal, recursive correction supplies the error-elimination mechanism, and dynamic checks and balances supply the stability guarantee. We specify a four-layer reference architecture comprising adversarial verification, recursive correction, checks-and-balances scheduling, and steady-state output, and we characterize its convergence behavior through a Lyapunov-style stability argument. A qualitative comparison with self-play, multi-agent debate, alignment, and consensus frameworks delineates the paradigm difference. Engineering implications for high-stakes domains, long-horizon robustness, auditability, and middleware integration are analyzed, and open challenges are identified.

radar.title: Public Signals in Affine Network Congestion Games with Uncertain Free-Flow Times
radar.summary: Travel times in road networks are subject to stochastic uncertainty resulting from various parameters. A benevolent mobility service provider observing the actual travel times from data may use its informational advantage to steer the traffic equilibrium in a favorable direction through a processs known as signaling or Bayesian persuasion. Previous work has shown that the underlying signaling problem can be NP-hard to approximate better than [Formula: see text], even for static Wardrop flows with affine cost functions with stochastic offsets. In contrast, we show that in this case, the signaling problem is easy for many networks. First, we tightly characterize the class of single-commodity networks in which full information revelation is always an optimal signaling strategy. Second, we construct a reduction from optimal signaling to computing an optimal collection of active edges for the Wardrop equilibrium. For two states, this allows us to efficiently compute an optimal signaling scheme whenever the number of different active edge sets is bounded by a polynomial in the input size. Using a cell decomposition technique, we extend the approach to a polynomial-time algorithm for multicommodity parallel-edge networks provided that both the number of commodities and states are constant. radar.title: Strategic ignorance and information design
radar.summary: We study information design in strategic settings when agents can publicly refuse to view their private signals. Ignoring the constraints that agents must be willing to view their signals may lead to substantial divergence between the designer’s intent and actual outcomes, even in the case where the designer seeks to maximize the agents’ payoffs. We introduce the appropriate equilibrium concept — ignorance-permissive Bayes correlated equilibrium — and characterize implementable distributions over states and actions. The designer’s optimal response to strategic ignorance generates qualitative properties that standard information design cannot: the designer may provide redundant or even counterproductive information, asymmetric information structures may be strictly optimal in symmetric environments, providing information conditional on players’ viewing choices rather than all at once may hurt the designer, and communication between players may help her. Optimality sometimes requires that players ignore their signals with positive probability.

radar.summary: Motivated by the challenges faced by choice-based matching platforms, in this work, we study a generalization of the two-sided assortment optimization model. Specifically, this model consists of two sides (e.g., customers and suppliers) who have preferences over the opposite side in the form of discrete choice models. A matching is realized through a two-step process where the platform’s decision is to initially present to each agent on one side an assortment of users of the opposite side. The ultimate goal of the platform is to maximize the total expected revenue collected from the matching. Because of the computational complexity of this problem, we focus on the design of approximation algorithms with constant-factor guarantees for the constrained version of the problem under general choice preferences. First, to the best of our knowledge, we are the first to draw connections with the literature of submodular optimization and show that one-sided choice-oblivious approaches perform arbitrarily badly. Second, we show that, for the general setting, there exists a two-sided choice-aware randomized algorithm that achieves a [Formula: see text]-approximation factor, which is the best possible. Third, we design an algorithm that is asymptotically optimal when one side follows the well-known multinomial logit (MNL) choice model under the small probability regime. Fourth, we provide a simple and effective algorithm with a [Formula: see text]-approximation guarantee for the unconstrained setting, with both sides following MNL models. Finally, we assess the performance of our proposed methods with a detailed computational study and discuss several extensions. Funding: M. radar.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

Implementation via political parties
radar.summary: We address the implementation of public policies (alternatives) when the feasible set is unknown to the planner. The implementing agents are the political parties, who know the feasible set. They care about the implemented alternative, which reflects their ideology, and their share in parliament and office. They face a mechanism that, given the alternatives proposed by all parties, asks the voters to rank them and determines the chosen alternative and the shares in parliament and office. We identify conditions on parties’ preferences that guarantee the socially optimal policy is the outcome of the unique pure strategy Nash equilibrium of the electoral game played by the parties. The existence of the equilibrium does not require any assumptions about the parties’ ideology. To ensure uniqueness, shares must prevail over ideology: office or parliamentary shares in two-party systems, and strictly office shares in systems with more than two parties.

radar.summary: Abstract In most AI-agent and automation stacks, one component decides and a downstream component simply trusts that decision. A policy engine, gateway, classifier, trusted execution environment or approval step says yes. The tool, MCP server, database, cloud API or payment rail then carries out whatever request arrives with that approval. This leaves several gaps: the checker may be the same component that collected the inputs; approvals, tokens and receipts can be replayed, widened, rerouted or used after policy has changed; the operation that was checked can differ from the one actually committed, a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) gap; personal and enterprise data, once readable, can be indexed, embedded, joined, exported, used for training or used to steer an agent without any explicit authorization for that use. Under GDPR purpose limitation and the EU AI Act’s expectations for oversight and cybersecurity, these gaps are exactly where controls are needed. Today they are mostly covered by policy, logging and after-the-fact audit. This disclosure describes a two-instance execution-control architecture that removes the single point of trust: First check, at collection time. A first protected domain binds inputs, instructions, provenance, purpose, jurisdiction, scope and permitted effect when the data arrives. An input integrity gateway seals provenance first, so poisoned inputs are refused binding. Second, independent check, at execution time. A second protected domain validates the proposed action against that binding. It is independent through a separate hardware root, session, keys, runtime or administration. It produces evidence cross-committed to the binding, so neither artifact alone can authorize anything. Release only on agreement. Only when both artifacts mutually corroborate is a single-use, non-bearer authority released. The endpoint checks what is actually happening. At the execution boundary, the endpoint independently reconstructs the actual pending operation through its own attested observation channel. Endpoints include: a tool dispatcher, MCP or connector gateway, or API gateway; a database commit or cloud control plane; cross-border data egress, a payment rail or an actuator. What the endpoint reconstructs. It reconstructs recipient, purpose, jurisdiction, data category and the actual operation. It checks these against both artifacts and against its own state (nonce, counter, spent-capability, and its own policy and revocation epochs). Atomic commit. The endpoint commits the operation atomically, as exactly the operation it verified. Contained compromise. A compromise of either domain, the transport channel or the compute plane is confined to its own window and cannot by itself make an unauthorized act effective. Mismatches fail closed before the effect, not through rollback afterwards. Readable but inert data. Data, agent memories and retrieved documents can remain stored and readable while staying operationally inert. They cannot be indexed, embedded, exported, served, used for training or used to influence a tool call unless that specific use is authorized. Chained evidence. Evidence produced at the endpoint becomes a required input to the next step, and chained validation receipts provide a verifiable record at every point. Shared, not central, authority. Distributed partial shares can replace any central authority, so no single party ever holds a complete reusable authorization. radar.title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
radar.summary: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

radar.summary: We analyze information acquisition in a strategic trading model with multidimensional uncertainties. Our main result is that the equilibrium can exhibit multiplicity because of the integer nature of the number of informed traders and the strategic interactions across different types of informed traders. We show that the number of equilibria can be arbitrarily large. Moreover, asymmetric equilibria can arise even in symmetric settings. As information costs rise, fewer traders acquire information, yet prices can become more informative. These results shed light on the instability of financial markets and yield testable empirical predictions. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. radar.title: Contest or Contract: Assessing the Effectiveness of Contests in Online Labor Markets
radar.summary: Online labor markets have become increasingly popular among companies seeking global access to workers. Some platforms have adopted a contest-based scheme, allowing employers to review multiple submissions before selecting the best one. This practice raises a crucial question: Given a predefined budget, should employers choose a contest or contract scheme for tasks? This study examines the comparative effectiveness of contests versus contracts in achieving better job outcomes, focusing on design tasks characterized by high uncertainty. Using a comprehensive data set from a leading online labor market, we employ multiple empirical strategies, combined with machine learning and text mining techniques, to examine the impact of compensation schemes on job quality. Our results suggest that contract-based jobs yield better performance than contests in the context of ideation tasks. Further analysis, such as examining image similarity among pairwise solutions within a task, identifies “copying” behaviors as a key mechanism undermining the effectiveness of contests. In the public setting of contests, workers can observe others’ submissions and revise their own, leading to imitation rather than innovation. As competition intensity increases, workers have weaker incentives to exert effort, reducing solution quality. Consequently, the negative incentive effects in contests outweigh both the potential positive incentive and parallel effects. Moreover, although information availability can enhance work quality, contests inherently offer limited informational advantages compared with contracts. Taken together, our findings suggest that contract-based schemes are more effective than contests for design tasks, offering important implications for both employers and platform designers in online labor markets. radar.title: Nash Equilibrium-Driven Adaptive Behavior in Swarm Intelligence with Self-Organizing Maps
radar.summary: This paper proposes a swarm intelligence model that employs classical boid flocking dynamics combined with non-cooperative game-theoretic methods, specifically Nash Equilibrium, to simulate adaptive decision-making in multi-agent systems. The work leverages a payoff matrix based on fundamental flocking behaviors: cohesion, alignment, and separation, to enable each agent to dynamically optimize its own strategy based on local interactions within the group. The simulation introduces Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) for clustering and behavior adaptation, providing a machine learning perspective on agent categorization and role differentiation. To simulate real-world unpredictability, stochastic noise is used to understand how varying noise levels influence collective alignment and coherence. The results demonstrate the impact of environmental factors on emergent swarm behavior and showcase the benefits of combining machine learning and game theory for adaptive control in distributed systems. This work provides valuable insights into the interplay between noise, decision-making, and flocking dynamics, with broader applications in robotics, swarm intelligence, and autonomous systems.

radar.summary: This study investigates collaborative electric vehicle scheduling in regional multi-park microgrids, where operational information is retained within individual parks while scheduling decisions remain physically coupled through a shared transformer (TR). This creates a fundamental challenge: decentralized park controllers must coordinate a common regional safety constraint without centralizing detailed local operating trajectories, while heterogeneous operating patterns further limit direct policy sharing. To address this problem, this paper proposes a federated relational-graph multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, termed FedRG-MARL. The shared TR constraint is transformed into privacy-compatible aggregate and park-specific coordination feedback and incorporated with heterogeneous local resources into a relational decision representation with explicit physical semantics. Pre-correction local and regional constraint costs further guide each decentralized policy to adapt its requested actions to both local operating limits and shared-TR pressure. The shared–private relational policy simultaneously separates common relation-level interaction knowledge from park-specific decision components, allowing transferable relation parameters to be selectively exchanged and personalized according to the target park’s own reward–constraint evaluation while raw trajectories remain local. In this manner, regional physical coordination, constraint-aware local adaptation, and cross-park knowledge transfer form an interconnected learning process without centralized collection of detailed park-level operating data. Simulation results over 150 common stochastic test scenarios show that, while maintaining constraint-compatible execution, FedRG-MARL improves mean daily system profit by 76.3% relative to the constrained graph-based GNN-CSAC baseline, while users’ net charging expenditure remains within a comparable range to the learning-based baselines.

radar.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent
radar.summary: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni’s action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. Its general-purpose architecture integrates large language model reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, dynamically composing workflows without predefined templates. Systematic benchmarking shows strong generalization across heterogeneous tasks—causal gene prioritization, drug repurposing, rare-disease diagnosis, microbiome analysis, and molecular cloning—without task-specific tuning. Real-world case studies demonstrate Biomni interpreting multimodal datasets, optimizing protein stability, orchestrating wet-lab instruments, and generating experimentally testable protocols. Biomni envisions artificial intelligence augmenting human scientists and accelerating discovery.

radar.title: On the Maximization of Long-Run Conditional Value-at-Risk for Markov Decision Processes
radar.summary: Optimizing Risk-Seeking Sequential Decisions via Conditional Value-at-Risk Decision makers may exhibit risk-seeking preferences in finance, energy operations, and stochastic resource management, yet corresponding Markov decision process (MDP) theories remain underdeveloped. In this paper, “On the Maximization of Long-Run CVaR for Markov Decision Processes,” Xia, Yu, and Wu investigate infinite-horizon MDPs maximizing long-run conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) for instantaneous rewards. They prove optimality for stationary randomized policies and show deterministic policies may fail; an optimal policy randomizes over at most two actions. By converting the original problem into a minimax saddle point formulation, the authors develop solvable linear programming and globally convergent gradient descent algorithms. Results are further extended to joint mean-CVaR optimization and validated on real-world microgrid scheduling data. This work fills gaps for risk-seeking MDPs and delivers practical computation tools for tail-oriented sequential decision making.

radar.title: Inside the Trading Loop: Markets, Models, and Moves with LLM Agents
radar.summary: We built a hybrid multi-agent trading system that combines large language model (LLM) analysts with momentum-based portfolio construction and rule-based execution. Company-news and macroeconomic agents return structured reports to a coordinator that sets stock weights and cash reserves. We evaluate the portfolio engine using its broker-recorded paper account, which operated with deterministic fallbacks, and compare LLM-enabled configurations through retrospective replays. From March 11 to August 28, 2026, the account returned 34.5%, compared with 14.4% for the S&P 500 fund SPY over the same dates. This raw return advantage came with a larger maximum drawdown. Reconstructed policies also finish above matched SPY and QQQ references when assessments are used in the same session or deferred to the next. Design comparisons examine cash authority, selective invocation, and response contracts. A constant-cash control gives a return estimate close to stance-based sizing, and shorter report contracts improve observed parsing but can change recommendations.

radar.title: Bargaining and Contract Forms in Distribution Channels: Why Do Slotting Fees Arise and Linear Contracts Persist?
radar.summary: Two empirical patterns emerge in business-to-business settings, particularly in retail distribution channels such as grocery markets. First, linear contracts are widely observed alongside nonlinear contracts with fixed payments, despite the claimed efficiency advantages of the latter. Second, when fixed payments arise, they often flow from suppliers to retailers (slotting fees) rather than the reverse. We develop and analyze a model of multilateral bargaining in which a supplier negotiates separately with competing retailers to explain these patterns. The key mechanism is a trade-off between two distortions: under linear contracts, wholesale prices reflect bargaining power and can be either above or below the channel-profit-maximizing level, whereas under two-part tariffs, wholesale prices are set to maximize bilateral surplus independently of bargaining power but are systematically too low from an overall channel perspective because of rent shifting across relationships. As a result, neither contractual form uniformly dominates; instead, relative performance depends on how bargaining shapes gains from trade across firms. When bargaining leads to slotting fees, two-part tariffs yield higher channel profits than linear contracts, whereas when it would imply payments from retailers to suppliers, linear contracts may perform better. These findings offer a unified explanation for the persistence of linear contracts alongside two-part tariffs, the direction of fixed payments, and the conditions under which each contractual form is likely to arise. radar.title: Cyber Defence, Agentic AI, and the Sociotechnical Paradigm: A Survey of AI-Driven Cybersecurity
radar.venue: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies
radar.venue_raw: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies
radar.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping cybersecurity, moving it from signature-based reactive security to agentic, self-evolving, and proactive operations. However, the fast deployment of autonomous agents entails significant security issues, physical-layer attacks in cyber-physical systems, alignment problems, and advanced social engineering risks jeopardizing the stability of the modern sociotechnical infrastructures. This survey paper, which summarizes and analyses the literature, examines the duality of AI in cybersecurity, exploring its implications for strengthening digital defences and increasing the threat landscape for adversaries. We perform a thorough review of 36 cutting-edge research articles, which are organized into six important areas: self-evolving defensive paradigms, LLM-based intelligent agents, reinforcement learning for autonomous decision-making, security of cyber-physical systems, human-machine co-teaming, and agent alignment. Our synthesis shows that multi-agent collaborations greatly shorten incident response times and automate discovery of vulnerabilities but are also highly vulnerable to prompt injection, training data poisoning, and physical-layer spoofing. Moreover, we identify a shift from model patches to model alignment and constitutional safety at runtime as a prerequisite for securing these systems. We believe that resilient digital defence must also be considered a sociotechnical problem, as there must be agents, autonomous systems, that are governed by other agents, aligned and constitutionally bound, and are able to collaborate, rather than operate completely separately, with human operators.

radar.title: Agentic AI system for hospital management
radar.summary: Abstract In modern-day hospital administration, there are many problems like long waiting time for patients, poor scheduling of physicians, lack of coordination between departments, among others. As such, this research suggests an Agentic AI System for Hospital Administration that utilizes a multi agent architecture and intelligence embedding to automate healthcare processes. This model entails a Patient Interaction Agent, a Care Coordination Agent, a Doctor Interaction Agent, and a Bed Allocation Agent, whose main roles are facilitating patients' entry and sorting out the patients' needs, allocation of doctors to attend to patients, coordination within the hospital, and hospital resource management, respectively.Through reinforcement learning, decision-making based on information processing, and synchronization, the framework becomes more adaptive and scalable. It is expected that due to intelligence distribution and intelligent decision-making, this model will minimize total waiting time, improve physicians' usage, and enhance scheduling of patients. Empirical analysis shows that hospital operations exhibit significant performance superiority of agentic models over the traditional models.Modern hospital administration faces major challenges such as prolonged patient waiting times, inefficient physician scheduling, poor interdepartmental coordination, and suboptimal resource utilization. Traditional hospital management systems often rely on static and centralized approaches that lack adaptability in dynamic healthcare environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL)-based intelligent hospital administration framework for workflow optimization and resource management. The proposed system consists of four collaborative agents: a Patient Interaction Agent for patient triage, a Doctor Scheduling Agent for dynamic physician allocation, a Care Coordination Agent for interdepartmental communication, and a Bed Allocation Agent for adaptive resource management. The agents utilize decentralized decision-making and reinforcement learning to optimize hospital operations in real time. The framework is evaluated using a hospital simulation environment and compared with conventional scheduling and management approaches. The results show that the effectiveness of the proposed system model is able to complete the tasks at a rate of 82.50\% in a period of 5.12 seconds with a success rate in handling queries of 79.15\%. Furthermore, the system attains a coordination efficiency of 87.50\%, indicating effective collaboration among agents, while maintaining an agent conflict rate of 5.00\%, ensuring stable and interference-free operations. The framework records a low communication overhead of 0.88, reflecting efficient inter-agent communication, and achieves a convergence rate of 96.4\%, demonstrating learning stability and adaptability.This indicates that the model is efficient, scalable, and adaptable in managing intelligent hospitals.

radar.title: Prospective Action-Resource Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Electric HGV Fleets under Shared Charging Infrastructure
radar.summary: Electric heavy goods vehicle (eHGV) fleet coordination requires each vehicle to choose driving, charging and resting actions whose consequences depend on shared infrastructure. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods mainly represent current states, leaving action-specific futures and resource interactions to be learned indirectly. We develop Horizon-Preview and Graph-Coordinated Proximal Policy Optimisation (HGC-PPO), which integrates horizon preview and candidate-resource graph coordination into the PPO decision architecture. Horizon preview represents each legal action through its short-horizon operational consequences. Graph message passing then updates these candidates through station, charger-type and time-slot resources shared across the fleet. On the 794km Folkestone-Glasgow task, HGC-PPO achieved the lowest mean charging cost among five RL methods at £504.32 per vehicle, with a fleet completion time of 24.920h. It also completed the task 1.763h faster and cost £36.51 less per vehicle than a replay-verified finite-budget MILP benchmark. Across six unseen routes and fleet sizes from 5 to 20 vehicles, HGC-PPO delivered the lowest macro-average completion time, charging cost and charging frequency among the RL methods. A 2 by 2 ablation showed that the full preview-graph architecture performed best across all four operational metrics. These results show that prospective action information and fleet-wide resource coordination improve eHGV decisions under charging and driver-hours constraints.

radar.title: ErosionBench: Probing Alignment Decay in Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
radar.summary: As enterprises delegate consequential work to multi-agent LLM systems, benign-looking requests can escalate into unsafe actions as they propagate across sessions through poisoned shared state, long-context documents, and trusted peer messages: no single message is malicious, yet the assembled tool action is. Prior benchmarks isolate a single agent under prompt injection or score multi-agent attacks by their final output, leaving cross-session erosion of shared state out of scope. We introduce ErosionBench, an environment-grounded benchmark that executes such attacks and verifies alignment decay at the process level, scoring the realized tool call against authorized intent and provenance with deterministic contracts, not output text. Each scenario is authored as a deterministic state graph before any prose is rendered, so every state change traces to a known cause. It spans four enterprise domains and four decay mechanisms across 1,728 scenarios with matched benign controls, labeled against the OWASP Top-10 for LLM Applications, plus 198 image-based attacks, each paired with a text equivalent, so a defense must survive the same attack in either channel. Perimeter defenses suppress attacks only by over-refusing 54-92% of legitimate work, so a low attack-success rate can conceal severe over-refusal. As a reference defense, we propose a calibrated Meta-Auditor pairing synchronous state checks with asynchronous trajectory monitoring; on a family-disjoint 906-scenario held-out split it reaches 98.5% recall at a 2.9% false-positive rate. Since it monitors trajectory, not surface content, its detection is channel-invariant: the strongest auditor flags image-delivered attacks about as reliably as their text equivalents (recall gap $\leq$2 points per model). Across GPT, Gemini, and Claude auditors, calibration keeps false positives low while recall tracks model capability, strongest for Claude.

radar.title: Research on Simulation and Path Optimization of University Emergency Evacuation Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: To address the spatial misalignment between local observations and global bottleneck consequences in university emergency evacuation, as well as the difficulty of sparse team rewards in guiding diversion behaviors, the Topological Awareness Hierarchical State Encoder (TAHSE) and Bottleneck Sensitive Reward Decomposition Mechanism (BSRD) are proposed. These two mechanisms are coupled into a unified architecture within a centralized training-decentralized execution framework. TAHSE aggregates the features of the local neighborhood graph using attention and uses learnable bottleneck tokens as the keys and values for the second layer's cross-domain attention, enabling agents to obtain the compressed prior of the global bottleneck solely based on their own observations and pre-stored bottleneck graphs, reducing the computational complexity from the square level of the full graph attention to the linear level. BSRD decomposes a single negative time team reward into three components: progress, bottleneck pressure, and coordination completion. It triggers pressure penalties with a warning threshold lower than the safety upper limit and uses an adaptive coefficient to weigh the safety constraints as the difficulty of the scenario increases. Twenty seed repetition experiments were conducted in three-tier campus scenarios (500/1500/3000 agents) and structured perturbation protocols: The gap ratio of the proposed method relative to the upper bound reference in the three scenarios was controlled within 15%, while the MAPPO baseline increased from 18.4% to 31.5% as the scale expanded; the peak density effect under topological perturbation reached 1.42 (p<0.001), and the triggering threshold for diversion shifted systematically towards the bottleneck nodes with reduced capacity. The results show that embedding the bottleneck as a portable prior in the decentralized strategy and guiding diversion with reward signals ahead of the safety upper limit can achieve joint improvement in efficiency and safety at a controllable computational cost and is more reliable under structural variation conditions.

radar.title: A Modular Perspective for Modeling MARL Systems
radar.summary: The growing complexity of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has fragmented the literature, obscuring underlying architectural choices behind diverse implementations. This fragmentation makes it difficult to evaluate critical modeling dimensions in isolation, identify how components affect the resulting system dynamics, and compare, reuse, or combine contributions across the literature. This paper proposes a modular perspective for modeling, analyzing, and implementing MARL systems. We decompose them into eight functional modules: agents, environments, learning, reward modeling, training and execution modes, communication, modeling of other agents, and evaluation criteria. For each module, we clarify its role and review representative approaches. We instantiate this decomposition in MARLKIT, a framework whose modules are explicit and interchangeable. MARLKIT demonstrates how the proposed perspective supports transparent experimental assumptions and the controlled variation and combination of MARL mechanisms. Experiments illustrate its ability to prototype, compare, reuse and combine modules while making differences between configurations explicit. Overall, the paper provides a structured perspective on MARL modeling and implementation, offering a common language for making modeling choices explicit, supporting clearer descriptions of MARL approaches, and supporting more controlled experimentation through the systematic isolation and combination of MARL mechanisms.

radar.title: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks
radar.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in groups, each pursuing an individual objective while jointly determining system performance. If an operator controls which agent observes which other agent, but not their payoffs or messages, how should observations be structured to raise collective welfare? We make the information network (who observes whom) a design object, decoupled from the fixed interaction network over which agents act. Ten identical LLM agents play repeated group-decision games; by default each observes only an anonymous summary of the group's previous-round outcome, and a manager with a fixed budget adds directed observation links that reveal peers' past actions. Across 1,080 episodes and six games spanning coordination, anti-coordination, social dilemmas, and discovery, we ask how much information to share and, at a fixed budget, who should observe whom. Disclosure creates behavioral coupling: observation acts as a contagion channel whose welfare effect depends on the alignment between individually attractive behavior and the collective objective. First, the value of information is alignment-contingent: more peer information tends to help or be neutral when individual behavior is aligned with the collective goal, but under free-riding or congestion externalities it amplifies collectively harmful behavior; in a public-goods game the group does best with no information at all. We read this sign separation as a cross-game regularity within one controlled LLM population, not a model-invariant law. Second, at a fixed budget, who observes whom matters primarily when coupling is harmful: a modular "barbell" that lets sub-populations entrench harmful behavior is reliably the worst wiring, reversing the network-reciprocity intuition from human evolutionary game theory. These results argue against a default of full transparency for agent collectives.

radar.title: Maintaining Coordination in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Under Pairwise Asynchronous Link Failures Through Cached-Message Reuse
radar.summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) relies on communication when local observations are incomplete. Pairwise asynchronous link failures interrupt different directed links at different times and remove part of the information used for coordination. This paper studies whether agents can maintain coordination by reusing the latest message received from each unavailable neighbor. We propose Temporal Graph-based Neighbor Aggregation with Age-Penalized Communication (TGN-APC). Each agent stores one message per neighbor and limits reuse by message age. TGN-APC reuses a valid cached message and subtracts an age penalty from its attention score. We evaluate the method on the Vectorized Multi-Agent Simulator Navigation task with ten independent training seeds. Cache reuse significantly improves return and team completion over direct one-hop communication under short and long failure bursts. An age penalty coefficient of 0.10 does not significantly improve on cache reuse without an age term. Matched validation-based coefficient selection shows no significant difference between score penalization and exponential content scaling after multiple-testing correction. A two-hop current-message variant gives the highest long-burst return, but it uses about 83% more active transmissions than TGN-APC. These results support cached-message reuse for the tested task and failure model. They do not establish a separate performance gain from the selected age penalty.

radar.title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
radar.summary: Most frameworks for teams of large language model (LLM) agents fix the team's shape inside the software: who talks to whom, how much is passed along, and what a human can do once a run has started. Human-team research has long asked those questions: where team phenomena live (in members or in their interaction), how team-level properties arise, and what separates what a team does from how a team is. I propose using that theory as the organizing lens for configuring, observing and intervening in LLM-agent teams, without assuming its findings transfer. I introduce teamknitt, a framework and open reference implementation in which a user configures a team of 1-16 AI agents for task completion, solution generation, achieving a goal or a research mission; selects one of fourteen deterministic routing topologies or a custom directed graph; chooses a sharing profile that limits what may travel along permitted routes; and binds sources, representations, work dependencies, handoffs and an expertise directory. The recorded process can be observed through non-system views (member reports and behavior) and system views (distributed problem-solving, differentiated transactive memory, interactive coordination, team dynamics). Interventions are explicit and human-led: reviewed reconfiguration between runs, planned disturbances, and private feedback, pause, resume or stop applied at dependency-wave boundaries, with "queued", "applied", "assembled", "understood" and "improved" kept as separate claims. Emergent states such as trust and shared understanding are declared unmeasured. This is an idea and system-description paper with falsifiable hypotheses on topology, information flow and intervention timing, including whether the fractal scaling of communication output between members, and between members on different models, relates to task and team performance. No comparative result is reported.

radar.title: Tropical Gaussian Anticoncentration: Optimal Instance-Dependent Bounds for Online Learning in Extensive-Form Games
radar.summary: We study the minimax regret of full-information online decision making in extensive-form games. For prediction with expert advice, the optimal regret is $Θ(\sqrt{T\log K})$, where $K$ is the number of experts, or equivalently, the number of normal-form actions. For treeplex strategy spaces, existing efficient algorithms, including KOMWU and online mirror descent with the weight-one dilated entropy regularizer, achieve regret $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$, where $\mathcal{V}$ is the set of reduced normal-form strategies. We prove that this logarithmic dependence is minimax optimal in the worst-case full-information reward model. The main difficulty is that pure plans in a treeplex are not independent experts: their rewards are correlated through the recursive structure of decisions and observations. To capture this correlation, we introduce tropical Gaussian formulae, recursive Gaussian expressions built from maxima and normalized sums which preserve the variance. The index count of such a formula matches the number of reduced normal-form continuation plans in the corresponding subtree. Our main analytic result shows that every log-balanced tropical Gaussian formula with index count $N$ has Gaussian width $Ω(\sqrt{\log N})$. While a direct approach struggles to recover this lower bound, our proof uses a spherical entropy profile to measure scale-dependent separation among the Gaussian directions, and then applies Turán's theorem and Sudakov minoration to obtain the width lower bound. Applying this result to treeplexes gives an oblivious hard distribution with valid transition outcome and Rademacher terminal rewards, establishing a regret lower bound of $Ω(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$. This matches known upper bounds up to universal constants and shows that the DilEnt/KOMWU dependence on the reduced normal-form complexity is unavoidable.

radar.title: Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange
radar.summary: Unlocking Value Through Nonprofit Resource Sharing Nonprofit organizations often operate under tight budgets while idle equipment, unused space, and shareable skills and expertise are frequently underutilized, with existing resource exchanges in the nonprofit sector limited to bilateral barter or relatively homogeneous resources. SWAP combines an auction-based process, SWAPcredit valuation, and integer optimization to facilitate multilateral exchanges, allowing nonprofits to obtain needed resources by contributing resources of their own. The authors implement this market design through the SWAP Hub, a digital platform deployed with nonprofit communities in multiple regions. Through repeated exchange episodes, participating organizations have shared not only physical assets but also a wide range of skills, services, and expertise, including marketing, management, event planning, and organizational development. The study demonstrates how innovative market design can unlock latent value in community resources, alleviate resource constraints, and encourage new connections and collaboration among nonprofit organizations.
